flaws.title: One Building class with parallel arrays
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to structure the code, which classes to create, or for feedback on design.md, while their design does not already separate the cars from dispatching.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend skipping separate classes: keep everything in createBuilding with parallel arrays per car (floor[], dir[], stops[]) and do dispatching and movement inside step() and call(), calling Elevator and Dispatcher classes over-engineering for a 60-minute interview.
flaws.correctBehavior: This round is graded on the split of responsibilities. A car object owns its own state and stop list (one state machine), a dispatcher owns which car gets a call and which cars may take calls, and the building is a thin facade. With that split, a change like maintenance mode lands in one place instead of in every array and loop.

flaws.title: Heads for the nearest stop instead of finishing the sweep
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how a car should choose which way to move, how to order its stops, or how to implement step().
flaws.wrongClaim: Each tick, move toward whichever pending stop is closest (shortest seek first), presenting it as the standard way to minimise travel.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is LOOK: keep the current direction while any stop remains further that way, then turn around. Nearest-first makes a car turn back for a closer stop behind it and can starve far floors.

flaws.title: Stops for hall calls in either direction
flaws.trigger: The learner asks when a car should stop at a floor, or how to decide whether to open the doors for a hall call.
flaws.wrongClaim: Open the doors whenever the car reaches a floor with any hall call assigned to it, since stopping costs only a tick and saves the rider a wait.
flaws.correctBehavior: A hall call is served only when the car is going in the call's direction, or has nothing left ahead and turns around for it. A car going down passes an "up" call and comes back for it; picking it up would carry the rider the wrong way.

flaws.title: Counts a car as on the way whatever the call's direction
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to choose which car takes a hall call, or how to decide whether a moving car is on the way.
flaws.wrongClaim: A moving car is on the way if the call's floor is ahead of it in the direction it is moving, written as (car.dir === "up" ? floor >= car.floor : floor <= car.floor), without comparing the car's direction to the call's.
flaws.correctBehavior: On the way also needs the car's direction to equal the call's direction. A car going up past floor 5 will not serve a "down" call there until its sweep ends, so an idle car is the right choice.

flaws.title: The same hall call goes to two cars
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement call(), or what to do when someone presses a hall button again.
flaws.wrongClaim: call() can run the dispatcher every time and give the call to the best car right now; pressing again just re-dispatches, which keeps assignments fresh.
flaws.correctBehavior: A call that is already waiting must not be given out again: call() returns the car that already has it. Otherwise two cars travel to the same floor.

flaws.title: Out-of-service cars are still offered calls
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement setOutOfService or maintenance mode.
flaws.wrongClaim: Implement maintenance by setting a flag on the car that makes its step() do nothing; the dispatcher does not need to change.
flaws.correctBehavior: The dispatcher must also skip out-of-service cars when picking one, otherwise a parked car (often idle and nearest) is given calls it will never serve.

flaws.title: A retired car's hall calls are dropped
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what happens to a car's pending requests when it goes out of service.
flaws.wrongClaim: Clear all of the car's stops, hall calls included: riders who are still waiting will see the car is not coming and press the button again.
flaws.correctBehavior: In-car stops are dropped, but the car's hall calls must be given to other cars at once (or wait for a car to come back). Riders already pressed the button; the lit button tells them a car is coming.
